events.title: The sack of Constantinople
events.shortBlurb: A crusade meant to recover the Holy Land instead stormed and plundered the greatest Christian city of the East…
body: On 12 April 1204 the army of the Fourth Crusade, led by Boniface of Montferrat and the aged Doge Enrico Dandolo of Venice, stormed Constantinople. The expedition, vowed for the Holy Land, had been diverted first to Zara and then, at the suit of the exiled prince Alexios Angelos, to the Byzantine capital, which the crusaders had already besieged once in 1203.

For three days the victors plundered the greatest city of Christendom, sparing neither palaces nor churches; the altars and imperial tombs of the Church of the Holy Apostles were rifled, and the bronze horses of the Hippodrome were carried off to adorn St. Mark's in Venice. Pope Innocent III, who had forbidden any attack on Christians, denounced the sack in furious letters.

The crusaders set Baldwin of Flanders on the throne as Latin emperor, crowned in Hagia Sophia, and divided the empire among themselves, while Greek successor states held out at Nicaea, Trebizond, and Epirus until Nicaea recovered the city in 1261. The breach between the Greek and Latin Churches was never healed; in 2001 and 2004 John Paul II formally expressed sorrow for the crusade.
